finding: The hub and the root landing advertise different pack sets, so a reviewer deciding from one surface sees a different inventory than from the other.
how_measured: regex over both files' href lists, intersected against ls docs/nfl-*/
measurement: docs/index.html links 16 pack ids; index.html links 14; hub-only: 309921cc, a411fed0, f4, market; root-only: e5e38f9e, wk. Directories on disk: 21 (incl. this pack)
why_it_matters: the decision layer the brief asks for assumes one canonical inventory; dfc0c1bc recorded the same drift as RF-02 and it is still live
action_taken_here: this pack added exactly one card to each surface (verified by tests/test_nfl_2dd0cbcb.py::test_hub_and_landing_reference_this_pack); the pre-existing 6-entry drift is left for the hub owner

finding: One pack ships build + checker + tests but has no CI workflow, so its gates never run on push.
how_measured: ls .github/workflows vs the docs/nfl-* pack dirs
measurement: 29 workflows; 21 pack dirs; missing: nfl-3b81013c-ci.yml (this pack's own workflow is added in the same commit as these findings)
why_it_matters: a green repository can hide an unchecked pack; regressions in that pack's data or pages are invisible
action_taken_here: logged only — not this pack's scope to add another session's workflow

finding: A prior pack's decision-readiness register contains an evidence pointer to a file that does not exist.
how_measured: extract every data/nfl_*/... pointer from data/nfl_a67ddef8/requirements.csv and stat each
measurement: 33 pointers, 32 resolve; dangling: data/nfl_6cefc476/announced_starters.csv (the file is at data/nfl_48217a55/announced_starters.csv)
why_it_matters: a readiness table is decision-grade only if the reader can open the evidence; today that is luck of authoring
action_taken_here: this pack's builder asserts pointer existence at write time and its checker re-asserts it (rule 6); proposed as a shared rule in 2DD-S13

finding: Another register cites a site page that was never built (docs/nfl-a67ddef8/flagged.html; the page is flags.html).
how_measured: grep for docs/nfl-*/[a-z]*.html inside data/nfl_a67ddef8/*.csv, then list the real directory
measurement: 1 dangling page reference; real pages: captures, flags, index, registers, reverification, sources
why_it_matters: dead links in a published register are exactly what the brief's verification rule is meant to prevent
action_taken_here: logged; that pack's data is not edited from this session

finding: Any file added to the tree invalidates data/assurance/inventory.csv, and the test that catches it is easy to trip mid-session.
how_measured: run scripts/audit_repo.py, commit more files, then run the harness; also a venv pytest run
measurement: harness reported 193/194 with the failure isolated to tests/assurance/test_audit.py::test_inventory_hashes_and_line_counts (720 passed, 1 failed under pytest at the same tree state); three further runs and the post-fixed-point run report 194/194
why_it_matters: the assurance gate works — it fails loudly on a stale inventory — but the fixed-point order is mandatory after every content change, not optional polish
action_taken_here: the fixed point (own pack twice, board twice, source coverage, audit, assurance) was run last in this branch, after all content existed

finding: The sandbox image has no pytest and no numpy/scipy, so whole-repo test counts are environment-dependent.
how_measured: python3 -m pytest -> 'No module named pytest'; .venv pytest after install -> 3 collection errors on tests/empirical (ModuleNotFoundError: numpy)
measurement: tools/run_tests.py: 194/194 (stdlib harness); pytest in a fresh venv without scientific deps: 720 passed, 1 failed, 3 collection errors, 6 subtests
why_it_matters: prior reviews quote pytest counts (502, 749) that cannot be reproduced here verbatim; publishing a number without its environment invites a false comparison
action_taken_here: this pack's tests are stdlib-only and run under both harnesses; the numbers above state their environment

finding: Cross-pack consolidation is filename-driven, so registers with non-canonical names are silently excluded from the board.
how_measured: src/nfl_dfc0c1bc/registers.py::is_suggestions_file / is_questions_file, then row counts per pattern
measurement: matched stems ingest 27 registers / 347 rows; 8 similarly-named files are skipped, including 3 real registers in other packs: data/nfl_0ce967db/desk_questions.csv (22), data/nfl_0ce967db/desk_suggestions.csv (18), data/nfl_0d4da02c/suggestion_options.csv (68) = 108 owner-facing rows never consolidated
why_it_matters: the board is where the owner chooses; a question that never reaches it is a question nobody answers
action_taken_here: this pack publishes questions.csv + suggestions.csv on purpose (tested: board grew 188->196 and 197->209, all rows themed, board verifier 15 rules / 0 failures); widening the stem rule is proposed in 2DD-S13's sketch

finding: daily-verify.yml has no schedule trigger, so nothing in the repo runs on a clock despite a name implying it does.
how_measured: grep -A3 schedule .github/workflows/daily-verify.yml -> no match; no 'on: schedule:' block in any nfl pack workflow
measurement: 0 scheduled workflows among the 29; capture cadence is session-driven
why_it_matters: requirements about 'snapshot every Wed/Thu/Fri' (R54) and 'automate immutable snapshots' (R29) cannot be called satisfied while cadence depends on a session happening to run
action_taken_here: R29/R39 left open with the reason recorded; a CI-first dry-run cron is proposed as 2DD-S09

finding: A root-level CSV named like an NFL ratings file is an NBA-era artifact.
measurement: 1 mislabeled-by-inheritance file; no NFL register in the tree derives ratings from it (checked the opponent-aware requirement's pointers)
why_it_matters: an opponent-aware ratings feature citing it would publish NBA numbers as NFL — the exact hallucination class the brief bans
action_taken_here: requirement R27 records explicitly that this file is not counted as NFL evidence

finding: Four assurance findings remain open at the baseline, three of them structural.
measurement: 17 findings, 4 open: A-F11 (verify_data checks internal consistency, labelled as source verification), A-F12 (legacy correlations lack qualification evidence), A-F14 (Korean statute article body not reproduced), A-F15 (no LICENSE file)
why_it_matters: A-F15 is a repository-level rights question only the owner can settle; A-F11/A-F12 change how much weight a reader should put on existing green check marks
action_taken_here: left open and cited here; this pack's pages label their own checks as transcription+arithmetic, never as source verification

finding: scripts/audit_repo.py cannot run on a shallow clone (it reads a base commit).
how_measured: git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository before/after the fetch started in this session
measurement: true at session start, false after 'git fetch --unshallow'; audit then completed in ~4s over 1,358 files
why_it_matters: a fresh session that runs the audit before unshallowing gets a confusing failure and may skip the gate
action_taken_here: documented in the review so the next session checks the flag first
